title: ansi-terminal build blocker: 'Not in scope: Underlining' in unix Internal.hs
description: Building zinc's optparse-applicative closure, 5/6 pkgs compile (colour [vendored], prettyprinter, ansi-terminal-types build OK). ansi-terminal fails: ansi-terminal/unix/System/Console/ANSI/Internal.hs: 'Not in scope: data constructor Underlining'. The reader correctly picked the unix (POSIX) source-dir over win32 (os(windows) conditional resolved). Underlining is a ConsoleLayer-family constructor from ansi-terminal-types' Types module; the dependent ansi-terminal cannot see it. Hypotheses: (1) our build of ansi-terminal-types did not expose ALL its modules (reader exposed-modules incomplete for this package), or (2) ansi-terminal needs additional cabal config (other-modules / autogen / CPP) we drop. ansi-terminal is also platform-heavy (FFI, conditional dirs) so more blockers may follow. Investigate ansi-terminal-types exposed-modules first. Blocks full zinc-builds-zinc (last package in the closure).

title: BLOCKER: colour (self-host transitive dep) has no git repo — git-native model gap
description: zinc's self-host closure: zinc -> optparse-applicative -> prettyprinter-ansi-terminal -> ansi-terminal + ansi-terminal-types -> colour. Verified: both ansi-terminal and ansi-terminal-types hard-depend on colour. colour (Russell O'Connor) is a darcs-era package with NO source-repository on Hackage and no git mirror found. The strict git-native fetch model (spec: pull straight from git, no Hackage at build time) therefore cannot resolve colour, blocking full zinc-builds-zinc (576.5). This is an ecosystem reality, not a zinc bug: some Hackage packages have no git repo. Resolution requires a design decision (Hackage-tarball fallback vs vendoring vs scoping self-host) — flagged to the user.
notes: RESOLVED (user decision 2026-06-04): vendor git-repo-less deps into git mirrors, keep strict git-only. colour -> create a git mirror from its Hackage tarball; point the self-host registry at it. Follow-up: host the mirror at a stable URL for clean-checkout self-host.
close_reason: Resolved via vendoring (user decision): colour-2.3.6 vendored from Hackage tarball into a git repo; builds cleanly via zinc as part of the optparse closure (build-type Simple, base-only leaf). Approach validated. Follow-up: host the mirror at a stable URL for clean-checkout self-host.

title: Resolver: handle real upstreams without zinc.toml (.cabal deps + workspace registry)
description: gitFetchManifest requires a fetched dep to have a zinc.toml; real Hackage packages have only a .cabal, so 'zinc add'/resolve cannot walk a real package's transitive deps (all self-host builds so far use a HAND-AUTHORED zinc.lock). For genuine 'zinc build' self-host: when a fetched dep has no zinc.toml, derive its deps from the .cabal (Zinc.Cabal reader) and resolve each dep's repo+subdir from the WORKSPACE [registry] (the per-project decentralized registry must list every non-boot transitive dep -> git repo[#subdir], since upstreams do not carry zinc registry info). Then 'zinc add' can freeze zinc's whole closure. Note: also needs a git repo URL for every transitive dep incl. colour (repo location TBD). Last capability gap before the self-host acceptance test.
close_reason: gitFetchManifest .cabal fallback (Opt-2 reader, ghc threaded) + resolver root-registry fallback for repos; hermetic fetch + resolve tests; 162 examples; -Wall clean. Resolver can now walk real upstream closures.

title: Pass cabal include-dirs to ghc CPP (custom headers)
description: Real package prettyprinter #include's a custom header (version-compatibility-macros.h) it ships under its cabal include-dirs. The Opt-2 reader does not extract include-dirs and buildLibArtifacts does not pass -I/-optP-I<dir>, so ghc's CPP cannot find the header: 'fatal error: version-compatibility-macros.h: No such file or directory'. Fix: extract include-dirs (Cabal BuildInfo.includeDirs) into Component, and pass -optP-I<pkgDir>/<incdir> (and -I) in the lib build. Surfaced building prettyprinter for self-host (zinc-576); blocks the optparse-applicative/toml-parser closure.
close_reason: Component.compIncludeDirs from reader+zinc.toml; -I/-optP-I passed in lib build; hermetic #include e2e test; 159 examples; -Wall clean. Real prettyprinter builds+links via zinc (Right 42).

title: Dependency subdir: build a package located in a repo subdirectory
description: prettyprinter and prettyprinter-ansi-terminal (needed transitively by optparse-applicative, a zinc dep) live in SUBDIRECTORIES of a monorepo (prettyprinter/prettyprinter.cabal), not at repo root. zinc clones a repo and expects the manifest/.cabal at the top level, so monorepo packages cannot be resolved/built. Add an optional subdir/path field on a dependency + lock entry (and registry) so the fetch points the build at <checkout>/<subdir>. BLOCKS self-host (zinc-576): the optparse-applicative closure needs prettyprinter*.
close_reason: url#subdir support: splitRepoSubdir + cloneAt clones url part + closure builder/manifest fetch read from <checkout>/<subdir>; unit + hermetic e2e tests; 158 examples; -Wall clean. Real prettyprinter resolves to subdir and compiles (new include-dirs blocker filed).

title: Refactor: ExceptT String IO to flatten Either-threading staircases

title: Level-parallel closure build scheduler
description: Build the closure level-by-level using topoLevels (zinc-n4r.1). WITHIN a level, compile nodes concurrently; ACROSS the level boundary, register serially. Required because: (1) ghc-pkg register into the shared workspace db is NOT concurrency-safe, (2) a dependent's compile needs its deps already registered. Split buildLib into buildLibArtifacts (fetch/compile/ar/write store conf, no register) + serial registerPackage. Concurrency via base forkIO + QSem (bounded by getNumCapabilities) to avoid adding async to the flake. Add -threaded + -with-rtsopts=-N to the zinc executable so subprocess builds truly overlap in production (runghc test harness is non-threaded, so it stays correct-but-serial). Depends on n4r.1.
close_reason: buildClosure builds level-by-level (topoLevels); parallel compile within level, serial register; buildLib split; parMapBounded tested; zinc exe -threaded -N; cabal build verified; 151 examples; -Wall clean

title: Evaluate Nix-NAR-compatible content hashing for store/cache interop
description: c3z.2 ships a self-contained deterministic tree hash (sha256 over sorted path\0content, excluding .git). Alternative: Nix-NAR-compatible 'sha256-<base64>' (via nix hash path) would let the zinc store interoperate with Nix cache semantics, at the cost of re-introducing a Nix dependency into the fetch/hash path (deliberately kept git-only). Revisit when the artifact cache (G1/G2) lands.
close_reason: Evaluated: keep the self-contained sha256 tree hash. Nix-NAR (sha256-<base64>) only matters for interoperating with Nix's binary cache, which zinc deliberately avoids — git fetches sources, Nix only provides the toolchain (spec §2). NAR-compat would re-couple fetching/hashing to Nix for no MVP benefit. Revisit only if a Nix-store binary-cache integration is ever wanted.
